column3: “Filthy” is rendered “rebellious,” and “which oppresses” “tyrannical.”
“Correction” is rendered “instruction”; NASB renders the perfects with “did not.”
“Officials” is rendered “princes”; “not gnaw to the morning” is rendered “They leave nothing for the morning.”
“Insolent” is rendered “reckless.”
“In the morning in the morning” is rendered “Every morning”; NASB adds “But.”
“Corners” is rendered “corner towers,” and “desolate” “in ruins”; “from not inhabitant” is rendered “without a man, without an inhabitant.”
“Fear” is rendered “revere,” and “visited” “appointed”; “rose early” is rendered “were eager.”
“For booty” is rendered “to the prey,” and “judgment” “decision”; “jealousy” is rendered “zeal.”
“A lip purified” is rendered “purified lips,” and “a shoulder one” “shoulder to shoulder.”
“Cush” is rendered “Ethiopia,” and “the daughter of my scattered ones” “My dispersed ones.”
“Practices” is rendered “deeds,” and “transgressed” “rebelled.”
“Afflicted and poor” is rendered “humble and lowly.”
“Injustice” is rendered “wrong,” and “disturbs” “make them tremble.”
“Shout” is rendered “Shout in triumph.”
“Your judgments” is rendered “His judgments against you,” and “enemy” “enemies”; “evil” is rendered “disaster.”
“Drop” is rendered “fall limp.”
“A warrior who will give victory” is rendered “A victorious warrior,” and “silent” “quiet.”
The Hebrew is difficult; NASB supplies “O Zion” and “of exile,” and renders “they were tribute on it reproach” as “The reproach of exile is a burden on them.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Their shame” is rendered “turn their shame into praise and renown.”
“Turn back your captivities” is rendered “restore your fortunes”; NASB adds “in” and “Indeed.”
